General

Article 77 (1) The Regent conducts supervision and evaluation of the implementation of women and child protection periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.

(3) The results of supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) constitute evaluation material for the policy of women and child protection programs in the Region.

Part Two
Prevention of Acts of Violence Against Women

Article 73
The family, in efforts to protect the rights of women, has the role to:
a. provide equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political, and cultural affairs;
b. prevent the occurrence of violations of women's rights in the household; and
c. protect women from conflict and violence in the household that degrades the dignity of women.

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Buol Regency. 2. Regional Government is the head of the Region as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of Government Affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Buol Regency. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Buol Regency. 5. Women's empowerment is an effort to enable women to obtain access and control over resources, economic, political, social, and cultural so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 6. Women's protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthy and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence, and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children who are still in the womb and are not married. 9. Prevention is direct efforts made by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 11. Children's forum is a forum for children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitment and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 13. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social. 14. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens so that they can live properly and are able to develop themselves, so that they can carry out their social functions. 15. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 18. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or suffering that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 19. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who holds control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries. 20. Complaint handling is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 21. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 22. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement statutory regulations. 23. Focal Point PUG is OPD apparatus who have the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 24. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of providing assistance to witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive. 25. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out skills assistance/guidance activities to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 29. Article 71
(1) Community participation in efforts to protect women and children:
a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of programs to prevent violations of the rights of women and children;

Letter a Sufficiently clear Letter b What is meant by gender justice is fair conditions and treatment towards women and men, in order for justice towards women and men to be realized, steps are needed to stop things that politically and socio-culturally can hinder women and men from being able to play a role and enjoy the results of that role.

Letter d Sufficiently clear Letter e What is meant by non-discrimination is that every woman and child without exception has the right to receive services related to the violence they experience, no one may be rejected or given priority over others except on the basis of certain emergency considerations.
Letter f Sufficiently clear Letter g Sufficiently clear Letter h Sufficiently clear

Article 20

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear.

Paragraph (2)
Point a What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and be able to empower victims.
Point b Sufficiently clear.
Point c What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.
Point d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service provision process must be kept confidential and known only by people who are relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to victims.
Point e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service providers must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems.
Point f What is meant by respecting individual differences (individual differences) is that each individual must be viewed as unique; each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism), so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any matter.
Point g What is meant by not judging is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information that comes from the victim will not be assessed or judged.
Point h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/actions to be taken.
Point i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in language understood by the victim. Lately, more and more disabled/difable/disable women have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or those experiencing mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be drawn from special school (SLB) teachers.
Point j What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delays due to the involvement of various parties; however, with the proactive nature of service officers, victims must be guaranteed to be able to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral cover letter. Efforts must be made so that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to their identity or case narrative.
Point k What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to put oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus victims feel accepted, understood and can openly tell their problems.
Point l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and the full exercise of their rights to survival, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination and participation, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.

RIGHTS OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Prevention of Acts of Violence Against Women

Article 20

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear.

Paragraph (2)
Point a What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and be able to empower victims.
Point b Sufficiently clear.
Point c What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values and social status.
Point d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service provision process must be kept confidential and known only by people who are relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to victims.
Point e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service providers must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems.
Point f What is meant by respecting individual differences (individual differences) is that each individual must be viewed as unique; each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism), so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any matter.
Point g What is meant by not judging is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information that comes from the victim will not be assessed or judged.
Point h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/actions to be taken.
Point i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in language understood by the victim. Lately, more and more disabled/difable/disable women have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or those experiencing mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided who, for example, can be drawn from special school (SLB) teachers.
Point j What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delays due to the involvement of various parties; however, with the proactive nature of service officers, victims must be guaranteed to be able to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral cover letter. Efforts must be made so that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to their identity or case narrative.
Point k What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an empathetic attitude, namely the ability to put oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus victims feel accepted, understood and can openly tell their problems.
Point l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and the full exercise of their rights to survival, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination and participation, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.

Health and Social

Article 32
